column1: # Spec 59 known differences: a case XLibur is known to answer differently from Excel. function, case id, xlibur answer, excel answer, reason, issue.
# A row must carry a reason. The runner fails on a row that now agrees, and on one whose XLibur answer changed.

column5: AND("") is #VALUE! in Excel and TRUE in XLibur
Overflow of a double: Excel returns #NUM!; XLibur throws ArgumentException
Excel refuses COUNTIF with a non-reference first argument at entry; XLibur accepts it and returns #VALUE!
DATE(1900,0,31) is #NUM! in Excel and serial 0 in XLibur
Overflow of a double: Excel returns #NUM!; XLibur throws ArgumentException, so IFERROR never reaches its fallback
Overflow of a double: Excel returns #NUM!; XLibur lets infinity through as a number
Number to text: Excel gives the 15-significant-digit plain decimal form; XLibur gives a different form (0.1+0.2 is 0.3 in Excel, 0.30000000000000004 in XLibur)
Number to text: Excel gives the 15-significant-digit plain decimal form; XLibur gives a different form (1/3 is 17 characters in Excel, 18 in XLibur)
Number to text: Excel gives the 15-significant-digit plain decimal form; XLibur gives a different form (1E-5 is 0.00001, 7 characters in Excel, 5 in XLibur)
Number to text: Excel gives the 15-significant-digit plain decimal form; XLibur gives a different form (18 characters in Excel, 22 in XLibur)
Excel counts an emoji (surrogate pair) as one character; XLibur counts UTF-16 units. LEFT and FIND in XLibur already treat the pair as one
Excel returns 9E307 for the median of two 9E307 values; XLibur throws ArgumentException (probably summing before halving)
Excel indexes an emoji (surrogate pair) as one character; XLibur indexes UTF-16 units and splits the pair
Excel returns #NUM! for MOD(1E15,7); XLibur returns the remainder
Excel returns #NUM! for MOD(1E20,7); XLibur returns the remainder
Excel returns #NUM! for MOD(3,1E-20); XLibur returns the remainder
Excel returns the real cube root for a negative base with exponent 1/3; XLibur returns #NUM!
Overflow of a double: Excel returns #NUM!; XLibur throws ArgumentException
Excel rounds 1.005 to 1.01; XLibur rounds the binary value to 1 (Excel probably rounds the 15-digit decimal form)
Overflow of a double: Excel returns #NUM!; XLibur throws ArgumentException
Excel returns exactly 0 for SUM(0.1,0.2)-0.3; XLibur returns the IEEE residue
Number to text: Excel gives the 15-significant-digit plain decimal form; XLibur gives a different form (0.1+0.2 is 0.3 in Excel, 0.30000000000000004 in XLibur)
VALUE("5-") is #VALUE! in Excel; XLibur parses it as -5
Approximate VLOOKUP on unsorted data: Excel returns the row for 2, XLibur returns #N/A
